Allergy.Flow: Patient-level allergy status and transactions own reaction/history rows. The reviewed save updates status, prevents duplicate allergy entries, replaces reactions on edit and writes deletion history. AllergyID is type-dependent drug/ingredient/allergen context, not a universal product FK. Patient-summary views can display these longitudinal records without a visit-owned transaction.

BedMgt.Flow: Visit/patient bed assignment checks existing visit assignment, occupied/blocked/deleted bed, updates bed status/gender and room gender, writes companion and bed/transaction logs, clears reservation indicators and calls VM accommodation. Transfer/unreserve are separate operations. Shared bed/hospital structure setup is not owned by a visit.

Billing.Flow: Product/category/UOM and contractual setup feed service price inquiry. Each visit service has its billing transaction; package sales create purchased snapshots with separate member/header/assignment identities. Tax and contractual state are part of the pricing cycle; payment and invoice synchronization belong to additional flows. Do not refresh purchased terms from current package master setup.

BloodBank.Flow: Patient donation and blood-unit inventory are distinct from a visit blood order and dispense transaction. Product/component/type/UOM/warehouse configuration drives unit handling. Reviewed dispense guards order status, returned state and expiry; expiry can discard the unit and conditionally add an investigation service, with transaction logging. Full compatibility, return and witness branches need targeted review.
BloodBank.Evidence: BloodUnitManagerFactory.DispenseBloodUnit921-1007; sample BloodUnit36 and order/log patient/visit anchors.

CN.Flow: Clinical notes copy patient/visit context and use type/status/cancel setup. Add stamps draft/sign/cancel dates according to status and copies actor display name; replies reject a cancelled note. The reviewed patient-summary note view selects signed status2 and nondeleted rows, so absence there does not establish missing storage.

CPG.Flow: CPGVisit and CPGVisitNeed represent master treatment-plan visit definitions and their configured needs/products/UOMs. VisitId here refers to CPGVisit.ID, not directly to VisitMgt.Visit. Setup deletion soft-deletes specialties, diagnoses, objectives, physicians, visit definitions and needs. Patient execution must be traced through its CPOE treatment-plan linkage rather than deleting these shared definitions.
CPG.Evidence: CPGSetupManagerFactory.DeleteCPG127-195; GetCPGVisits(cpgId); visible FKs and samples.

CPOE.Flow: Orders connect visits/patients to product classification, accepted quantity and execution instances. OrderlineID links are version/family-dependent. Medication administration, lab/rad investigation, nursing performance and dental execution are downstream writers, with conditional VM charges. Package expansion differs for IPD versus other classifications. Order sets and treatment-plan setup are shared definitions.
CPOE.Evidence: visit-evidence-study.md; module-source-findings.md; two sampled MedicationOrderSetLine parent misses in fk-sample-evidence.json.

CS.Flow: Form/category/configuration setup feeds patient clinical-sheet records and state. Reviewed add checks the form and sets draft/sign state and timestamps; edit selects an existing draft and uses ModifiedTS; cancellation selects a signed sheet and sets cancel reason/comment/date with concurrency control; soft deletion is a separate operation. Related-visit retrieval can display episode sheets. The merge handler updates identity/display fields for transferred visits.

DBA.Flow: Database monitoring owns blocking, size, index, query and restart diagnostic data. Visible monitoring procedures include blocked-session/heavy-query/missing-index collectors. These are infrastructure records, not owned patient/visit/product children; SQL text/plan payloads can contain sensitive content and were excluded from data samples. Exact scheduling/retention is not inferred from table names.
DBA.Evidence: SQL object metadata, safe/presence samples and visible DBA procedure list.

dbo.Flow: Mixed schema: contains legacy core views/order caches, import/staging tables, script work tables, backups and diagnostic snapshots. Names such as dummy, Temp or dated backups do not prove active use or safe deletion. Resolve the actual writer and consumer per table; some effective Security permission views live here. No single dbo business cycle can be inferred.
dbo.Evidence: Full table samples; SQL object dependency catalog; Security live views; original visit study.

DotcarePortal.Flow: Jobs portal audit writes ActionLog header and per-row ActionLogDetail in a local SQL transaction after execution; logging failures are best-effort and do not prove a job failed. JobToggle controls job availability and PortalAdmin is a separate portal admin list. VisitId in audit detail is an execution reference, not clinical ownership. This is different from the migration portal protected store.

Drug.Flow: Drug schema is configuration, frequency/duration reference conversion and MediSpan request/response logging, not the primary medication master. Reviewed patient mapper combines requested patient/drugs, configured previous-order range, CPOE previous orders and renal lab values before normalization; home-medication/current-visit rules differ. Request/response payloads were not sampled.
Drug.Evidence: DrugDB PatientMapperManagerFactory.Map42-132; configuration/key and safe log-state samples.

ER.Flow: Triage patient transaction can precede a registered patient/visit; samples include a null PatientID. Regular ER and virtual ER paths have different extension requirements. Acuity/arrival/room/disposition configuration feeds the visit/order path; clinical and billing rows must be traced from the resulting visit rather than treating every triage row as a Visit extension.
ER.Evidence: Original visit classification source/sample study; ER safe samples.

Finance.Flow: Visit billing feeds invoice/service/tax and payment synchronization; VMPaymentTransaction wrapper attempts payment then visit invoice synchronization, with a suppressed-transaction recovery branch. Journal entry editing is limited to draft/unposted state, validation/fiscal period/account setup drives details, posting writes history and can be automatic for zero-period journals. Reversal mapping swaps debit/credit and retains account/owner/cost center context.

FreeChat.Flow: Chat owns its local user projections, chats, threads and messages. Reviewed pharmacist-physician chat resolves the physician through Security, creates missing local user projections, reuses/creates a visit-specific chat and matches order lines to threads. Message payloads are outside this study. Local chat-user records are not Security.User rows.

HangFire.Flow: Job/state/queue/parameter/counter/hash/list/set/server tables support background work. Reviewed UIUtilities startup selects Hangfire SQL storage, starts a server, configures automatic retries and registers the recurring message-queue error-handling job using configured interval/retry limit. Its SHR replay behavior is separate from deleting a business record. Other job producers and serialized arguments require job-specific review.
HangFire.Evidence: UIUtilities Global.asax37-59; MQErrorHandlingManager29-170; safe state/presence samples.

HR.Flow: User-confirmed sync entry is HR.Proc_SyncData (job inactive in test). It reads per-entity source profiles, conditionally establishes linked servers, stages organization units then positions then employees, maps local to universal identities and applies staging to main HR tables. MaxId/LastUpdatedDate configuration supplies watermarks. TransactionType1/2 are applied and become3. Termination derives from last termination record; security user bindings remain a distinct layer.
HR.Evidence: Live definitions of seven Proc_Sync procedures; security-flow.md; HR repository active/nonterminated filters.

HSM.Flow: Hospital structure hierarchy, beds and assignment type/classification determine projection routing. Reviewed room save writes HSAssigment, refreshes OPD medical nurse-station specialties, updates BedMgt copies, removes old ER/OR projection when classification changes and calls the new classification owner. Delete guards nurse-station use, deactivates assignments/deletes specialty links and calls ER/OR removal. This study does not implement deferred setup migration.
HSM.Evidence: HospitalStructureManagerFactory room-save815-965 and delete1101-1183; assignment samples/lookups.

itreports.Flow: Mixed operational extension/reporting schema, including admissions/consents/communications/AI/report caches. It is not read-only by definition: reviewed custom procedures insert package details and PowerApp admission projections or directly change goods-receipt/visit status. Some procedures hardcode entity/UOM/actor values and are not general migration adapters. Consumer apps, refresh and payload retention must be identified individually.
itreports.Evidence: Six visible custom stored procedure definitions; SQL dependency map; all-table safe/presence samples.

LR.Flow: Product investigation/component/sample/template setup drives patient/order-instance investigations. Result save checks ModifiedTS concurrency, persists results, attempts completion transition and appends history for successful noncompleted saves. A final-result projection selects result type2 and aggregates the latest result date; IsDeleted<>1 excludes SQL NULL, unlike ISNULL(...,0)=0. Lab/rad/micro and device result branches require their own status guards.

MedHistory.Flow: Patient longitudinal social/family/symptom/obstetric/medication/surgical sections also carry visit context and separate logs. Reviewed save replaces existing rows for supplied nonnull sections and appends corresponding logs; social marital status may update MPI. Medication history is not equivalent to an active CPOE prescription. Profile/log tables are another aggregate.

MedStp.Flow: Specialty hierarchy and physician master feed visit/order/schedule caches across modules. Physician contacts/qualifications/specialties belong to the master aggregate; exactly one main specialty and supervisor compatibility matter in reviewed import. Physician flags do not provision HR or Security users. Renames require writer-specific cache handling, not blanket replacing all text.
MedStp.Evidence: Physician-Integration.md; original specialty confirmations and target metadata/samples.

MPI.Flow: Patient master owns reviewed registration address/contact/relationship aggregates and lookup-derived demographics; identification validation and MPIConfiguration govern input rules. Patient merge moves selected visit references and publishes cache updates to consumers such as CS/Allergy. Corrected import, merge and longitudinal history deletion are distinct operations. Search indexing is a separate postcommit effect.
MPI.Evidence: Patient-Direct-Import.md; Security and CS source evidence; MPI safe samples and prior registration study.

NewDental.Flow: Product/category/procedure mapping plus chart/treatment-area/numbering setup drives patient dental transactions. Add validates active patient treatment areas and applicable procedure mapping, writes audit/visualized status and creates CPOE orders for nonplanned items. Perform can create a VM service for insured state, updates CPOE instance to in-progress, then local status/audit. Planned procedures are not automatically charged services.

NP.Flow: Nursing order/dispensed-item/perform records connect order instances, product/UOM, visit, service and optional warehouse. The reviewed perform path compares total performed versus requested/charged quantities, dispensed origin and service-kit presence to decide VM charging or local perform-only. Bed accommodation/milk/OR/discharge records are separate subcycles, not all children of one perform transaction.

Nphies.Flow: KSA-specific authorization/claim/communication/reconciliation owns request-response transactions and historical item/attachment snapshots. Reviewed claim logging copies patient/contract/visit context and item OrderLineId, ServiceId and ProductId and stores bundle file references. Cancellation sends external tasks, logs errors and updates visit NPHIES status; local deletion is not cancellation of the payer request. External acknowledgement was not executed/tested.

NS.Flow: Notification type/template/configuration and recipient/entity context drive persisted notifications. Reviewed writer validates payload/template/type, commits notification creation then publishes IDs to clients; routing can target all entities, one entity or explicit entity list. Local row persistence does not prove delivery. Email/template/event/attachment paths are separate from this websocket notification path.

OPD.Flow: OPDPattern recurrence and generated instances support physician schedule/booking/arrival. Housing is separate. Pattern recurrence is also parsed by BIReport views; schedule changes can affect QMS and PhysicianDesktop pattern-instance projections. Booking, reschedule/cancel and historical visits must preserve already consumed schedule relationships.
OPD.Evidence: OPDPattern-Integration.md; original OPD visit source study; QMS booking source; BIReport definitions.

OR.Flow: Reservation links patient/visit, room and operation products, with status history. Save creates/edits CPOE operation order, copies product category display data and calls VM according to reservation configuration. Product-specialty/anesthesia/duration/room setup influences the cycle. Cancellation and performed-operation financial behavior are not a generic reservation delete.

PA.Flow: The only visible base table is ICD10(ICDDiagnoseCode), but 14 views compose stock balance/price, OPD/IPD visit/service/authorization and physician scheduling data from SC, Billing, CPOE, VisitMgt, MPI and OPD/MedStp. These are projections rather than extra owned visit tables. CPG_Policy uses the ICD code reference; no integer identity should be invented for it. Exact view predicates remain source-specific.
PA.Evidence: PA SQL object column/dependency contracts; base-table presence samples. No standalone patient-admission master inferred from abbreviation.

PatPrlm.Flow: Patient/visit chief complaints, diagnosis problem cards and detail/history records connect ICD setup to visit diagnosis caches. Add can update MPI marital status for maternity, writes cards, synchronizes VM diagnosis code/name and checks treatment-plan relevance. Dated BKP tables also exist and are not automatically live clinical ownership.

PhysicianDesktop.Flow: Desktop assignments are polymorphic left/right items typed by SLKP_Relation, not universal physician FKs. Add prevents duplicate physician/specialty/nurse-station assignments and copies labels; access list combines Security physician roles, assignments and the current physician. Widgets/configuration query patient/visit source projections; they do not own the underlying clinical history.
PhysicianDesktop.Evidence: AssignmentTransactionManagerFactory.AddAssignmentTransaction32-133; widget manager entry points and table samples.

Physiotherapy.Flow: Visit/patient order -> product-specific order details -> scheduled/performed sessions. Perform validates quantities, state and unique CPOE order linkage, creates session and calls VM then CPOE before success. Scheduling, partial session execution, cancellation and rescheduling are distinct states; remaining quantity is not merely a service-row count.

PMGT.Flow: Classification-specific product/drug projections serve clinical consumers and use category/UOM/reference-unit caches. Core master product setup is shared, while patient consumption belongs to order/service/stock records. Goods-receipt validation publishes product updates to PMGT; delivery/replay consistency is a separate integration check.
PMGT.Evidence: Product-Drug-Integration.md; original product samples; SC GoodsReceiptRSDNotificationMangerFactory.

QMS.Flow: Outpatient booking creates/reuses pattern-instance details and a patient booking with queue-model-dependent code. Cutting/rebooking marks old booking deleted and may reuse its code. VM arrival/cancellation updates and clinic-state integration are separate actions. Queue/monitor/SMS effects are not reproduced by inserting appointment rows alone.
QMS.Evidence: GenerateQueueCodeManagerFactory.SavePatientAppointmentBooking74-129; source callback entry points; safe samples.

reports.Flow: Mostly functions/views/procedures over source domains, not owned transaction tables. Base tables include ActiveEntity and linked_visits. Reviewed stock functions calculate quantity/cost from barcode/balance/transfer states and UOM conversions. One current-quantity function assigns a single warehouse-location variable; one last-cost function uses a global TOP1 over the supplied list. Do not assume these are universally correct multi-location/multi-product reconciliation helpers without checking input scope.
reports.Evidence: Selected live SC report function definitions; 822 SQL object contracts; all base-table safe samples.

SC.Flow: Product/category/UOM/warehouse/vendor setup feeds procurement, receipt, balances, transfers, dispensing and returns. Reviewed validated receipt updates PO details/status, batch barcodes, location balances in reference UOM, average cost, Finance journal linkage and PMGT events; Saudi RSD is conditional. Active insert triggers generate barcode/code and transfer/return prefixes. Direct row imports must account for generated values and postcommit external effects.
SC.Evidence: GoodsReceiptRSDNotificationMangerFactory.SaveAndValidateGoodsReceipt150-314; live three SC trigger definitions; product integration evidence.

Screening.Flow: Questionnaire is a visit/patient capture aggregate that orchestrates MedicalHistory, diagnosis, Allergy and MPI marital-status services before saving its local snapshot children. Success of a questionnaire is not independent of these domain writers. Deleting only Questionnaire cannot reverse longitudinal medical-history updates already made.

Security.Flow: Actor identity and entity context apply across patient/visit/product domains. Backend API and frontend page-action permission chains share Permission/Role grants, with static/admin/version-dependent exceptions. Additional entity assignment controls navigation, not automatic combined visibility. Shared EntityID0 is mainly setup/config; copied employee/physician bindings and token/menu state require refresh-aware handling.
Security.Evidence: security-flow.md and security-evidence.json; user-confirmed entity rule.

SerLoc.Flow: ServerService and ServiceAction map an action name to base URL+relative URL and method. Reviewed locator retrieves the row and builds the proxy from these values; a missing action fails and the reviewed proxy rejects calls to a module marked optional. Endpoint configuration affects every cross-module callback; it is not owned patient/visit data. Logs can contain payloads and were excluded.
SerLoc.Evidence: ServiceLocatorModel.GetServiceProxy50-108; ServiceProxy optional-module branch109-121; table relationship samples.

Shared.Flow: Shared static vocabulary/configuration and cross-module repository views provide contracts for visit/order/product/billing consumers. Shared SLKP classifications are application enums, not independently generated IDs per import. Repository views do not imply duplicated writable tables. Entity-specific operational filtering still depends on the consuming writer/repository.
Shared.Evidence: Static vocabularies; Shared DAL source view repository inventory; SQL dependency catalog.

SHR.Flow: ErrorMessage stores failed message envelope, original queue/exchange/routing, pending/published/stopped/exception state and retry count. Reviewed UIUtilities job first republishes pending DB rows under the configured retry limit, then consumes the broker error queue into SQL. Duplicate checking uses an in-memory OriginalQueue+Message dictionary, not a durable global uniqueness guarantee. Payloads were excluded and no replay was executed.
SHR.Evidence: MQErrorHandlingManager.ConsumeErrorQueueMessages29-108, RepublishMessageFromDB110-124, SaveErrorMessageToDB130-170, PrepareErrorMessageModel264-280; model maps SHR.ErrorMessage.

VisitMgt.Flow: Visit classification dispatch, visit details, service/order caches, billing/tax, package assignment/consumption, accommodation, financial state and invoice synchronization are distinct but connected cycles. Patient/product/physician masters are referenced, while extensions/history and service effects need owned-record tracing. OPD/IPD/AMB/ER plus virtual ER and package behavior differ.
VisitMgt.Evidence: visit-evidence-study.md, core-flows.md, 120-query cohort, original package/service evidence.

VS.Flow: Vital-sign/BMI setup includes measurement type, limits, age/sex ranges and indicators. Transactions can be patient-scoped or visit-linked. Reviewed external-device path validates time/duplicates/ranges and derives normal-range status before saving. Patient-summary projections group visit/timestamp measurements and expose derived display rows with NEWID, not stable base-record IDs.
VS.Evidence: VitalSignTransactionManagerFactory.AddVitalSigns1302-1395; live PatientSummery vital view and cohort.

BIReport.Flow: Read-only schedule projection: two views parse FREQ/INTERVAL/BYDAY recurrence strings from current and temporary OPD pattern tables. They are neither separate schedule masters nor patient-visit records. Safe recurrence-ID samples connect this schema to OPD setup.
BIReport.Evidence: Two live view definitions and projection samples.

Gateway.Flow: Statement service/diagnosis/lab/vital projections compose insured visit/service/tax, financial contract and report-display mapping for external gateways. Reviewed SumServiceTax filters active insured services with CompanyShare>0 and nondeleted tax; it is not a universal all-visit tax total. Zero rows for selected samples can reflect these filters.
Gateway.Evidence: WSL_StatementData_Service and SumServiceTax live definitions; projection sample query.

impreports.Flow: Investigation turnaround/final/cancel timing projections combine LR/CPOE and visit classification. Final-result date view groups by investigation with ResultType2 and IsDeleted<>1; null deletion flags have SQL three-valued behavior. These are derived timing views, not result-write ownership.
impreports.Evidence: Live LR_GetLastFinalInvestigationResultDate and VW_VM_GetVisitIdByClassification definitions; safe classification samples.

PatientSummery.Flow: Patient/visit summary projections compose allergy, notes, sheets, problems, histories, medications, investigations, operations and vitals. View naming is not ownership: reviewed allergies-per-visit is patient-level, notes filter signed2, histories UNION six sections and vitals derive grouped rows with NEWID. Some display rows have no persistent identity and should never be delete targets.
PatientSummery.Evidence: Ten reviewed projection definitions/columns/dependencies and safe projection samples.

Interpretation: Schema-level study findings. Explicitly unresolved branches remain unresolved; two-row samples do not establish exhaustive correctness.
